newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 5.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 5.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 5.00 cents higher Thursday as traders expect the market to bounce back from Wednesday's late-session sell-off.
"There was a lot of selling at the close, but more people are still friendly to the market," said one trader.
Traders said London's failure to make $200 lower due contributed to New York's higher call.
"London was due $200 lower and it didn't go anywhere near it," said another trader in New York. "We're due 5.00 higher based on numbers."
London coffee futures were lower early Thursday. By the midday break, September slumped $51 to $1,620, traded $1,648 to $1,607. November fell $41 to $1,621.

Wednesday, New York arabica futures erased sharp gains and ended mostly lower, pressured by a late bout of speculative selling. September settled down 3.15 cents at 185.75 cents a lb after ranging from 198.00 to 185.00. December slumped 4.70 cents, to 161.35 cents, while the back months closed down 2.25 to up 3.05.
The September/December switch widened to 24.40 cents compared with 22.85 cents at the close on Tuesday.
Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 190.00, followed by 195.00 and 198.00. Support was seen at 184.50 cents, followed by 183.
After Wednesday's close the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 875 60-kg bags as of July 29, to 92,649 bags. An additional 4,504 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.
On the weather front, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Thursday that there is no damaging cold weather expected during the next seven days in Brazil's coffee belt.
WSC said colder weather is expected over Argentina next week. At this time, however, this cold air is not expected to move northward into the coffee belt, it said.
